question.problem:
Let $S$ be the boundary of the finite solid region enclosed by the planes $y=-1,$ $y=1,$ $z=0,$ $z=2,$ and the surfaces $x=y-z$ and $x=1+{y}^{2}.$ Given that the surface $S$ is positively (outward) oriented and $F=i+x{z}^{3}\,j+xz\,k,$ the flux of $F$ across $S$ can be written as 

$$

question.worked_solution:
Let $R$ be a simple solid region bounded by a closed surface $S$ with positive (outward) orientation. If a vector field $F$ has continuous partial derivatives for all its components in an open region in space that contains $R,$ then the divergence theorem states that

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}\text{div}\,F\,\text{d}V.
$$

Computing the divergence of $F,$ we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{div}\,F & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(1)+\frac{∂}{∂y}(x{z}^{3})+\frac{∂}{∂z}(xz) \\  & =0+0+x \\  & =x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, using the divergence theorem, we have

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∭}_{R}x\,\text{d}V,
$$

where $R$ is a type II solid region that can be written as

$$
R=\{(x,y,z)\,:\,-1\le y\le 1,\,0\le z\le 2,\,y-z\le x\le 1+{y}^{2}\}.
$$

As a result,

$$
\begin{aligned}{∭}_{R}x\,\text{d}V & ={\int }_{-1}^{1}{\int }_{0}^{2}{\int }_{y-z}^{1+{y}^{2}}\,x\,\text{d}x\,\text{d}z\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$
